title: Connecting with Indigenous STEM talent
summary: The Phillips 66 Native American Network recently represented the company at the AISES National Conference.
body_markdown:
During Native American Heritage Month, Phillips 66 recognizes the contributions of Indigenous employees, including members of the Native American Network who recently represented the company at the AISES National Conference


*Pictured left to right:* *Jason Morin,* *manager, ops excellence, Ferndale Refinery;* *Melina Ivie,* *senior advisor, public affairs, Ferndale Refinery;* *KiLee Watson, analyst, experience recruiting, human resources;* *Lacy* *Hamilton,* *senior manager,* *analytical* *solutions, energy* *research* *and* *innovation;* *Brenda Shumate,* *vice* *president,* *midstream* *operations;* *and* *Josh Linn, director, technical, Ferndale Refinery.*


In October, members of the Phillips 66 Native American Network joined refining and midstream colleagues at the[2026 AISES National Conference](https://conference.aises.org/) , hosted by the Advancing Indigenous Science and Engineering Society (AISES) in Portland, Oregon.


They connected with Indigenous students, professionals, educators and employers across North America to share expertise on AI’s evolving role and strengthen relationships that support the company’s operations and communities.


**Why it matters**


Experiences like this provide opportunities to support Indigenous STEM talent, share technical expertise and connect with students and professionals from communities connected to the company’s operations.


- For tribal nations, AISES provides high school, undergraduate and graduate students options to gain access to career and educational opportunities, compete in academic and research competitions and attend culturally relevant professional development sessions.


- For Phillips 66, engaging with students and the Indigenous community helps us better understand community priorities, while also building talent pipelines for a future-ready workforce.


Phillips 66 at AISES


“Strong relationships with tribal nations are built through listening, respect and transparency,” said Brenda Shumate, Native American Network global sponsor and vice president of midstream operations.


> “These opportunities strengthen our shared commitment to safe operations, environmental stewardship and long-term trust.”
>
>
> Brenda Shumate


Those principles were on display throughout the conference, where employees shared expertise, explored emerging technologies and engaged with the next generation of Indigenous STEM professionals.


Phillips 66 had the privilege of:


- Supporting students: Phillips 66 sponsored four travel scholarships to help Native American students attend the conference.


- Sharing expertise: Brenda Shumate, Lacy Hamilton and Jason Morin, moderated by Melina Ivie, led a panel discussion exploring how artificial intelligence shapes the future of work and engineering in particular.


- Building connections: Employees connected with students, professionals and industry leaders at the Phillips 66 College and Career Fair, sharing information about the company and career opportunities.


Listen and learn


The Native American Network’s participation reflects the important role they play in supporting Indigenous talent, strengthening cultural understanding and building meaningful relationships with tribal communities.


Employee Resource Groups like the Native American Network help power our community. They foster connection, belonging and professional growth across our workforce and create opportunities to build community and celebrate different perspectives.


Phillips 66 works with tribal nations across its refining and midstream footprint. The opportunity to participate in AISES strengthens understanding, fosters meaningful dialogue and builds relationships with communities connected to the company’s operations.


Meaningful engagement starts with listening and learning from others, values that are at the heart of the company’s broader approach to two-way stakeholder engagement. Learn more about how Phillips 66 engages the communities we serve with a[One Team Approach](https://www.phillips66.com/safety/stakeholder-engagement/) .
